prompt:
Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, brushed by hand in black ink. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the drawing changes. The second reference image only shows the costume, the face and the proportions of the character: do not copy its drawing style, its colours, its outlines or its three-view layout. The third reference image only shows the ink technique of the game: do not copy anything of its content.

Drawing technique: traditional East Asian ink brush painting of a figure (sumi-e): the character is drawn with a few confident calligraphic strokes of black ink that swell and taper, some breaking into dry-brush streaks, and filled with flat washes of diluted grey ink: the dark fur (arms, legs, the eye stripes, the back of the head) one dark wash, the cap and the vest one medium grey wash, the satchel and the parcel one pale grey wash; the shirt, the white face stripes, the ears' rims and the belly are left as bare white paper. The only colour is the scarf: one flat wash of vermilion red with a few darker red strokes for its folds and fringe. No other colours at all: no green, no brown, no cream. Simple, bold shapes, no fur texture, no knitted pattern, no hatching, no smooth shading, no glossy highlights; eyes as small black dots, the nose one black dot. The same stroke width, the same ink tones and the same level of detail in every figure. Not a pen drawing, not a cartoon with uniform outlines, not a 3D render, not a watercolour in many colours.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

The figures are isolated on a fully transparent background: everything outside the figures is transparent; the bare paper inside each figure (shirt, white face, belly) is opaque white. No paper texture or paper colour outside the figures, no ground line, no shadow on the floor, no seal stamps, no text.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

A study sheet of separate single brush marks in black sumi ink on plain flat white paper, to be cut out as effect elements for a 2D game. Every mark stands alone with generous empty white space around it; no mark touches another or the edge of the sheet. Row one: three long horizontal strokes of a wide, half-dry brush, each starting with a pressed rounded head and ending in a tail of dry-brush streaks with flecks of white paper, in three ink tones: pale grey, medium grey, black. Row two: four short, slightly wavy horizontal ripple strokes in pale and medium grey, as used to suggest small waves on water. Row three: three soft, rising, curling wisps of very pale grey wash with feathered edges, like thin smoke from a chimney, each about as tall as a stroke in row one is long. Row four: three small flying seabirds, each made of only two or three curved black strokes for the wings (wings raised, wings level, wings lowered), and two round dots of black ink of different size.

Technique: real ink brushed by hand on absorbent paper: strokes swell and taper with the pressure of the brush, edges bleed slightly, dry-brush streaks are visible; ink only, no colour, no outlines around the marks, no shading. The paper is pure flat white without texture, fibres or shadows, evenly lit. Not a digital vector drawing, not a 3D render.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

No seal stamps, no calligraphy, no characters of any script.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
